title: AMD Helios Architecture Deep Dive: The Power of AMD's Hardware Combined
gist: AMD's Helios rackscale AI system is now in production, combining EPYC 9006 'Venice' CPUs, 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs, Pensando NICs/DPUs and ZT Systems rack engineering into 2.9 EFLOPS of MXFP4 compute, 31TB of HBM4 and 1.7PB/s of aggregate memory bandwidth - with per-GPU bandwidth landing about 21% above AMD's own year-ago projections. Note that despite the article URL slug referencing Broadcom, the text names no Broadcom hardware: the networking silicon described is AMD's own Pensando, making this a story about AMD's four-year vertical-integration bet paying off.

themes.theme: Rackscale as the new unit of compute

insights.claim: The unit of AI infrastructure has shifted from the server to the rack because AI workloads exceed what a single server can supply in both processing power and memory capacity.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Vendors selling discrete servers or components are being disintermediated by whoever can sell the whole rack; procurement decisions and margin pools move up a level.
insights.quote: rackscale systems have come to the fore as AI workloads are too large for a single server, both in terms of processing power and memory capacity
insights.locator: Increasingly serving as the backbone of datacenter AI hardware

insights.claim: Rackscale clustering is identified as a key reason NVIDIA gained its position in GPU computing, framing Helios as AMD's attempt to neutralize a structural rather than a chip-level advantage.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The competitive battleground is system integration, not FLOPS per die - which means NVIDIA's moat is attackable only by a vendor with CPU, GPU, NIC and rack engineering in-house.
insights.quote: It is a computing paradigm that, in part, has helped put AMD rival NVIDIA in GPU computing space.
insights.locator: The next step beyond a single server

insights.claim: The hard part of rackscale is execution rather than concept, since the underlying principles are straightforward and supercomputer clusters long predate them - the differentiator is adding fabrics to GPUs and building networking hardware to extend those fabrics across a rack.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Screens out paper competitors: only vendors shipping working scale-up fabric silicon should be credited with rackscale capability, regardless of announced roadmaps.
insights.quote: The technology principles behind a rackscale system are reasonably straightforward, and simpler supercomputer clusters have existed long before them. Still, the execution needed to make a rackscale system work is another matter.
insights.locator: The technology principles behind a rackscale system

insights.claim: Helios is the first product where AMD's CPU, GPU and DPU/NIC lines plus ZT Systems rack engineering ship as one integrated appliance, making it the proof point for AMD's whole acquisition strategy.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Helios is the single product on which AMD's AI-datacenter re-rating rests; execution slippage here invalidates the multi-year M&A thesis.
insights.quote: Helios is a culmination of multiple AMD technologies, CPU, GPU, and DPU/NIC, along with its ZT Systems engineering, into a single product

insights.claim: It took four years from AMD's 2022 Pensando acquisition until the networking pieces were in place for a true rackscale system, quantifying the lag between an infrastructure acquisition and a shipping integrated product.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A four-year integration lag is the benchmark to apply when pricing in the payoff from other semiconductor acquisitions - the market usually underestimates this.
insights.quote: After acquiring Pensando in 2022, four years later, all of the pieces are finally in place for AMD to strike out in the world with its first true rackscale system, Helios.

insights.claim: The named silicon content of Helios is entirely AMD's own - EPYC 9006 'Venice' CPUs, Instinct MI455X GPUs and Pensando NICs/DPUs - with no third-party networking vendor identified anywhere in the article body.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Contradicts the article's own URL slug implying Broadcom content; on the described configuration, merchant networking silicon vendors get no attach from a Helios rack.
insights.quote: The combination of AMD EPYC 9006 “Venice” CPUs, Instinct MI455X GPUs, and Pensando NICs/DPUs, Helios is the flagship technological achievement for AMD.

insights.claim: Helios and all its constituent parts are now in production rather than being a demonstration or roadmap item, following more than a year of AMD promotion.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Moves Helios revenue from forecast to near-term recognition; watch AMD datacenter GPU revenue for the ramp inflection over the next two quarters.
insights.quote: At long last, Helios and its constituent parts are now in production.

insights.claim: A Helios rack packs 72 GPUs delivering 2.9 EFLOPS of peak MXFP4 compute performance.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The 72-GPU rack count matches the prevailing rackscale reference configuration, making per-rack EFLOPS and $/EFLOPS directly comparable against competing racks.
insights.quote: The 72 GPU systems will offer 2.9 EFLOPS of peak MXFP4 compute performance.

insights.claim: Each MI455X GPU carries 432GB of HBM4 at 23.3TB/second, aggregating to 31TB of HBM4 memory and 1.7PB/second of memory bandwidth per rack.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: 432GB per GPU is an enormous HBM4 content per die - each Helios rack consumes 31TB of HBM4, making rack unit volumes a direct multiplier on HBM supplier revenue.
insights.quote: With those GPUs paired up with 432GB of HBM4 memory offering 23.3TB/second of memory bandwidth each, the cumulative rackscale system offers 31TB of HBM4 memory with a total memory bandwidth of 1.7PB/second.

insights.claim: Per-GPU memory bandwidth on the MI455X came in about 21% above what AMD originally projected a year earlier, and this was the single largest deviation from plan across the shipping specification.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A 21% bandwidth upside directly improves inference throughput per rack versus AMD's own guidance - a positive surprise that competitive benchmarks published on year-old AMD figures will understate.
insights.quote: the bandwidth per MI455X GPU (and thus the whole rack) is about 21% higher than AMD originally planned
insights.locator: That latter specification is also the starkest difference

insights.claim: Memory bandwidth, not compute, is identified as one of the major remaining bottlenecks in AI inference.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Supports overweighting HBM and memory-interface suppliers over pure logic scaling as the constrained input in the inference buildout.
insights.quote: With memory bandwidth remaining one of the major bottlenecks in AI inference, any improvement will be most welcome by AMD and its customers alike.
insights.locator: That latter specification is also the starkest difference

insights.claim: A year after first announcing Helios, AMD's shipping specifications came in remarkably close to its original projections, an execution-credibility signal for a company whose AI roadmap has been questioned.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Raises the weight investors should place on AMD's forward AI product claims; roadmap discount for AMD versus NVIDIA arguably narrows.
insights.quote: the shipping specifications for the system ended up being remarkably close to AMD’s original projections
insights.locator: Looking at the state of Helios a year after AMD first announced the rack

insights.claim: Helios provides 260TB/second of cumulative scale-up network bandwidth inside the rack versus only 43TB/second for scale-out beyond the rack, roughly a 6:1 asymmetry.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: The rack boundary is a hard bandwidth cliff, so workload partitioning and model-parallel strategies must fit inside 72 GPUs - and the inter-rack layer remains the opening for external networking vendors.
insights.quote: The scale-up domain offers a massive 260TB/second of cumulative network bandwidth between the nodes, while the scaling-out domain offers a more modest 43TB/second of bandwidth beyond a Helios rack.

insights.claim: Extending GPU fabrics with purpose-built networking hardware is described as the biggest advance that made rackscale systems practical, elevating fabric design above GPU design as the enabling technology.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Interconnect IP and switch silicon are where rackscale differentiation now lives - a reason to track fabric standards fights as closely as GPU launches.
insights.quote: the biggest advances in making rackscale systems a reality have been adding those kinds of fabrics to GPUs and then designing networking hardware to extend (scale up) those fabrics to connect to the other nodes within a rack
insights.locator: A rackscale AI system not only needs CPUs and GPUs

insights.claim: Helios was the highest-profile announcement at AMD's 2026 Advancing AI event and received the company's deepest public disclosure yet on its scale-up architecture.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: AMD is concentrating its AI narrative on a single flagship rack, so sentiment on AMD's AI position will track Helios customer wins more than component-level announcements.
insights.quote: by far the most high-profile was the semi-formal launch of AMD’s Helios rack
insights.locator: Of all the product announcements made at this year’s AMD Advancing AI event
